items.title: Bhotekoshi floods expose gaps in Nepal’s emergency communications
items.summary: Most mobile services have been restored, but damaged towers and fibre have forced operators onto slower backup systems as experts call for the implementation of a disaster communications plan drafted after the 2015 earthquake.

items.title: School students cut snack money to help Bhotekoshi flood victims
items.summary: The contributions, meant for flood-affected children, demonstrate that even small gestures can provide meaningful relief in times of disaster, teachers say.

items.title: Nepal flood survivors lack space even to mourn their dead
items.summary: Families perform funeral rites using effigies, mourners struggle to find cooking gas.

items.title: They escaped the 2015 earthquake. They couldn’t escape the Bhotekoshi flood
items.summary: After years of unfulfilled government promises to move them to safe ground, dozens of quake-affected families in Rasuwa and Nuwakot have now been swept away by the catastrophic Bhotekoshi flood.

items.title: Bhotekoshi floods halt Nepal’s electricity exports to Bangladesh
items.summary: Nepal had been exporting an average of about 1,000 MW of electricity during the wet season. That has now fallen to around 650 MW.

items.title: In Bhotekoshi’s wake, experts and activists question environmental cost of AI
items.summary: As Nepal considers setting up data centres of its own, experts say the country must assess their energy, water and environmental costs before breaking ground.

items.title: Oft-battered Langtang Valley cut off after Rasuwa floods
items.summary: The Bhotekoshi floods swept away roads and bridges linking Langtang with Dhunche, leaving tourists dependent on helicopters and raising concerns over supplies and the future of the trekking season.

items.title: 147 local representatives, government staff, teachers and security personnel missing after Bhotekoshi floods
items.summary: The missing include 83 security personnel and 64 local representatives and government employees, according to government data, as the overall number of people unaccounted for reaches 3,916.

items.title: Nepal’s political parties call for unity as criticism grows over flood rescue
items.summary: In the House of Representatives on Wednesday, leaders urged a coordinated response to the Bhotekoshi disaster as opposition parties criticised delays in tunnel rescues.

items.title: PM Shah addresses five queries over government’s handling of Bhotekoshi floods
items.summary: In Parliament, the prime minister defended the government’s response to the August 26 disaster, addressing criticism over warnings, body management, foreign assistance, tunnel rescues and coordination with provincial and local authorities.

items.title: Prime Minister Balendra Shah vows ‘courage and resolve’ as government faces mounting pressure over Bhotekoshi flood
items.summary: Prime minister tells parliament the disaster in Rasuwa, Nuwakot and Dhading is a shared national tragedy as the government details its search, rescue and relief efforts.

items.title: Nepal rescue teams race to reach workers feared trapped in hydropower tunnels
items.summary: Search crews are clearing debris, draining flooded tunnels and blasting through rock as operations continue at several projects in flood-hit Rasuwa and Nuwakot.

items.title: Bhotekoshi floods left 2.2 million tonnes of debris, UNDP estimates
items.summary: Preliminary estimate based on satellite imagery, damage assessments and engineering estimates.

items.title: Nepal sent its disaster alert 38 minutes after the glacier collapse. It wasn’t enough
items.summary: Some Nepalis survived the Bhotekoshi and Rasuwa flood by luck, not by warning. Their story, and interviews with the officials who built Nepal’s flood alert system, exposes their limits and shows how a knowable risk went unmonitored for years.

items.title: Bhotekoshi survivors reunited with families after five days
items.summary: Twenty-three workers from Bardiya, who narrowly escaped the flood in Rasuwa, returned home on Sunday after spending days stranded in the disaster zone.

items.title: Rescue teams struggle to reach workers trapped in underground powerhouses
items.summary: Families are demanding answers as mud and debris block access to hydropower plants where dozens of workers are feared trapped after the Bhotekoshi flood.

items.title: Nepal flood death toll rises to 1,127 as 4,858 remain missing
items.summary: Death toll from the August 26 flash flood continues to climb as search teams recover bodies downstream.

items.title: In Thecho, Matayaa becomes a festival of remembrance and satire
items.summary: This year’s procession honoured victims of the Bhotekoshi floods while continuing a tradition of using music, performance and satire to reflect on society.

items.title: Trade shifts to under-resourced Korala point after Rasuwa and Tatopani closures
items.summary: Customs officials seek additional manpower and equipment as traders divert stranded containers to the border point in upper Mustang.

items.title: Family performs funeral rites after Bhotekoshi flood victim’s body goes missing
items.summary: Raj Kumar Shrestha’s relatives say a body resembling him was photographed after the August 26 disaster but they were unable to locate it after they were told it had been transferred to TU Teaching Hospital from Nuwakot.

items.title: Authorities scramble for alternatives after Krishnabhir road cave-in
items.summary: A 70-metre section has fallen into the Trishuli river, and another 120 metres is severely cracked.

items.title: 1.6 million affected by Bhotekoshi floods, says government report
items.summary: Government’s first situation report puts the death toll at 1,050, with nearly 4,000 missing and more than 21,000 security personnel involved in a vast rescue operation alongside international teams.

items.title: UN Women estimates 43,000 women and girls in Nepal need urgent flood assistance
items.summary: An estimated 157,050 women and girls in Rasuwa and Nuwakot have been directly or indirectly affected, with food, safe water and protection emerging as urgent concerns.

items.title: Prioritise psychological support for those affected by the Bhotekoshi flood
items.summary: Counselling should extend beyond the worst-affected districts to places where affected people have relocated or come from.

items.title: The case for transparency in Nepal flood rescue flights
items.summary: When the flood washed away the roads, helicopters were the only way out. So why were politicians and camera crews hogging them?
